title: Accountant liability to third parties — Mercer & Co.
instructions: Mercer & Co. negligently (not recklessly) audited Fulton Inc. Fulton's CFO told Mercer that the statements would be given to First Bank for a loan. Decide whether each plaintiff can recover for its losses under the approach stated.

rows.label: First Bank, under the Restatement (foreseen users) approach
rows.explanation: First Bank was a known, intended user.

rows.label: An unknown investor who bought Fulton stock, under the Restatement approach
rows.explanation: Unknown investors aren't in the limited foreseen class.

rows.label: The same investor, under the foreseeability (Rosenblum) approach
rows.explanation: Any reasonably foreseeable user may recover.

rows.label: First Bank, under strict Ultramares privity (bank not a primary beneficiary)
rows.explanation: Without privity or primary beneficiary status, ordinary negligence claims fail.

rows.label: Fulton itself, for losses its own negligence did not cause
If Mercer had acted with reckless disregard, could the unknown investor recover even in an Ultramares state?
rows.explanation: Gross negligence (constructive fraud) extends liability to foreseeable users.

rows.label: Is compliance with GAAS an absolute defense to negligence?
rows.explanation: It's strong evidence of due care, not conclusive.
